ideas.title: The Paralyzed Pinky Glitch
ideas.angle: An interactive physical test where the viewer locks their hands together and finds it physically impossible to move their pinky. The glitch occurs due to tendon sharing in the hand, forcing viewers to try it, fail, and comment their results.

hook.en: You physically cannot move your pinky.

ideas.reason: Body-based interactive glitches consistently hit 100%+ APV because the viewer must pause or loop the video to perform the physical action. This specific tendon-locking glitch is a high-retention 'pattern interrupt' that creates instant physical engagement.
sources: Anatomy of the Extensor Digiti Minimi and Tendon Juncturae Tendinum
Physiological constraints of hand motor control studies

ideas.title: The 3-Second Nod Trick
ideas.angle: A dark psychology tactic where you nod slightly three times after someone finishes speaking. This micro-behavior triggers an evolutionary response that forces them to keep talking and reveal more information than they intended.

hook.en: Nod three times to control anyone.

ideas.reason: Practical 'power dynamics' content is currently surging on Shorts. This specific technique is actionable and provides a 'secret' social advantage, which drives high shareability and saves.
sources: The Definitive Book of Body Language by Allan and Barbara Pease
FBI behavioral analysis techniques for interviewers

ideas.title: The Gray Strawberry Glitch
ideas.angle: A visual interactive test showing an image of strawberries that contains zero red pixels. The viewer's brain 'hallucinates' the red color due to color constancy. It challenges the viewer to zoom in and see the gray, leading to high engagement.

hook.en: There is no red in this image.

ideas.reason: Visual illusions that claim a color 'isn't there' trigger immediate skepticism and the urge to 'prove the video wrong.' This drives viewers to re-watch the video closely and comment their disbelief, boosting VVSA and APV.
sources: Journal of Vision: Chromatic Adaptation and Color Constancy
